question:
A 24-year-old female presents to the ED with acute onset of pleuritic chest pain and shortness of
breath. She reports left lower leg swelling and pain over the past few days. Her only medication is oral
contraceptives, and she has no significant medical history. Physical examination reveals: -
Temperature: Normal - BP: 105/70 mm Hg - HR: 115/min - RR: 22/min - O2 saturation: 93% on room
air - Mild distress but generally stable - Clear lung sounds - Regular cardiac rhythm without abnormal
sounds - Left leg with 2+ edema Additional findings: - Covid-19 vaccinations current and SARS-CoV-2
test negative - ECG shows sinus tachycardia only - Negative pregnancy test Which diagnostic test
would be most appropriate for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Troponin measurement (B) D-dimer
testing (C) Arterial blood gas analysis (D) High-sensitivity CRP measurement (E) Transthoracic
echocardiogram (F) Exercise stress test (G) CT pulmonary angiography (H) Chest X-ray (I)
Ventilation-perfusion scan (J) Serum D-dimer testing
 A. Chest X-ray
B. Arterial blood gas analysis
C. Ventilation-perfusion scan
D. High-sensitivity CRP measurement
E. Troponin measurement
F. CT pulmonary angiography

G. Serum D-dimer testing
H. D-dimer testing
I. Exercise stress test
J. Transthoracic echocardiogram
